def: A cv-unqualified object type meeting Cpp17DefaultConstructible, Cpp17CopyConstructible, Cpp17CopyAssignable, and Cpp17Destructible; complex and valarray may be instantiated only with numeric types, and the behavior is undefined if operations on these types throw exceptions.

Collective term for the floating-point status flags (divide-by-zero, inexact, invalid, overflow, underflow) and floating-point control modes (such as rounding direction), read and written via <cfenv>. It has thread storage duration; a new thread inherits the creator's environment at the time the thread/jthread is constructed; whether FENV_ACCESS is supported is implementation-defined.

An object that consumes a sequence of integer data and, on request, produces any number of unsigned integers in [0, 2^32), used to supply initial state to random number engines; its generate may depend on the history of previous calls. std::seed_seq is the seed sequence provided by the standard.

A function object returning unsigned integers, each value in its range [G::min(), G::max()] being (ideally) equally probable; min/max must be static constant expressions with min < max. Since C++20 expressed by the concept uniform_random_bit_generator; the named requirement additionally needs a nested result_type.

A deterministic URBG that additionally meets requirements for seeding, equality comparison, and stream input/output. Its specification gives the size of the state, the transition algorithm TA, and the generation algorithm GA; two engines are equal if and only if the infinite sequences they will produce are the same.

An engine that takes the output of another engine (the base engine) and applies an algorithm to it to obtain different randomness properties, such as discard_block_engine, independent_bits_engine, shuffle_order_engine; its state includes the base engine's state, and base() returns the base engine.

A function object that, called with a URBG as argument, returns values distributed according to some probability density function or discrete probability function; it may have internal state (cleared by reset), and its parameters are bundled as param_type. The algorithms producing each distribution are implementation-defined, so results are not reproducible across implementations.

The algorithm TA by which a random number engine advances its state e_i to the successor state e_{i+1}; together with the generation algorithm GA it fully determines the engine's output sequence. e() advances to TA(e_i) and returns GA(e_i).

The value_type of the input/output mdspans and the Scalar template parameters in <linalg>; it must model the scalar concept composed of semiregular and others, and a value-initialized object must act as the additive identity.

Two mdspans overlap if there exist multidimensional indices for each such that the elements refer to the same object; if they have the same extents and refer to the same element index by index, they alias, which is a special case of overlap. Output parameters in <linalg> must not overlap other mdspan parameters unless explicitly permitted.

A type that can be an element of a std::simd data-parallel type: all standard integer types, character types, float and double, the defined float16_t/float32_t/float64_t, and complex whose components are vectorizable floating-point types.

All enabled specializations of basic_vec and basic_mask; consisting of a number of elements of the same element type, where the number of elements (the width) is constant for each type. The applications of an element-wise operation are unsequenced with respect to each other.

A type indicating the size and binary representation of a data-parallel object; together with the element type it determines the width. native-abi<T> is an implementation-defined tag that is the most efficient for the target platform, and deduce-abi-t<T, N> gives a tag with width N.

A std::simd term: a conversion from an arithmetic type U to a vectorizable type T is value-preserving if all possible values of U can be represented by T. Broadcast constructors and loads accept only value-preserving conversions by default; otherwise an explicit conversion or flag_convert is required.

C23 <stdckdint.h>'s ckd_add, ckd_sub, ckd_mul: compute a op b as if with infinite precision, write the result modulo-wrapped into *result, and return whether the mathematical result cannot be represented in the type of *result (i.e. whether it overflowed). In C++, all three types are required to be signed or unsigned integer types.
